newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki still breaking records, volume hefty.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki still breaking records, volume hefty.

text.p: Shares shrugged off some fairly determined profit-taking to push to a fourth straight all-time close in lively trade on Thursday, with Raisio still soaring and Nokia up but clearly off its intrasession highs.

The FOX index rose 0.92 percent to a record close at 1,220.76 points, while the all-share HEX index rose 0.97 percent to a record 3,532.87 points. Volume was again unusually heavy for a mid-July session at over 900 million markka.
Profit-takers focused on recent stars Nokia and Raisio, restraining overall gains, but brokers said this week's rally meant even some light losses on Friday would not spoil the mood.

"Before the weekend we could see some people taking home some gains at the end of such a strong week, but I don't see any big drop," one broker said, adding: "Overall I continue to be very optimistic about the market."

Nokia ended up 5.00 markka at 446.00 after rising almost four percent to a life-high 458.00 in brisk dealings. Some bulls said U.S. telecom infrastructure group Lucent's above forecast Q3 earnings boded well for Nokia's markets.
Raisio closed up steeply for a third straight session, gaining 75.00 markka to end at 640.00, but off a new all-time high 652.00, in heavy volume.
Brokers and analysts said prices around 640-650 markka were starting to look like consolidation levels for Raisio.

"To continue to bid it up, people would like to have more information about the deal with McNeil," one broker said, referring to Raisio's deal this week on a partnership with U.S. consumer goods giant Johnson & Johnson's McNeil unit.

But others said it was hard to see a ceiling for Raisio, which they said had moved well out of the usual range of Finnish price to earnings valuations. "This is now an American share, with a valuation like an U.S. stock," one broker said of Raisio.
